mechanism: Use an open red unit-square corner in A as source and the two existing unit-leg corners of the lower half-triangles in B as receivers. The intended error assigns each same-span receiver the full square area, overcounting B as 3 instead of2.
primary_unique_math_proof: Shoelace on the frozen original five polygons gives area2 for A,B,C,D,E. A consists of one unit square and two half-unit triangles. B consists of one unit square and two half-unit triangles. C does as well; D is half of a2by2 square; visual E is a diamond with diagonals2 and2. Therefore the choice E, all equal, is unique. The marked A corner has two unit legs bounding a full square. The B lower left and right corners each have unit horizontal and vertical legs, but each region is cut by its original diagonal, hence each area is1/2, not1.
